items.name: Orange-star stream beyond the spiral
items.subject: The same orange light and recognizable pale companions in a more bowed, spread strand.
items.distinction: Preserve the orange star's size and spectrum convention; changed arrangement, no fragmentation or extinguishing.
items.sourceMeaning:
The orange star is still shining. Almost every star passes between the other galaxy's stars, while their paths bend beyond the old spiral. A galaxy can lose its familiar shape without losing its lights.

*Orange-star stream beyond the spiral*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Gas crowded into the dark lane
items.subject: The same forked dark ribbon packed into a narrower, denser ridge with enlarged opaque knots and faint compressed edge.
items.distinction: No completed stellar population or complete young system yet; preserve the fork from a-lane-cloud.

fixedAssets.variantPolicy: Reuse registered source only where camera and creation state match.

items.sourceMeaning:
The clouds cannot slip through one another as the stars did. Their collision compresses and heats the gas. Radiation carries heat away, allowing the denser parts to gather further. Only some of this great cloud will become stars.

*Gas crowded into the dark lane*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A broad bridge of hot gas
items.subject: A broad smooth luminous span with ragged faint edges and a mostly knot-free interior.
items.distinction: Hot diffuse bridge, not solid bridge, fire, cold dense filament or strings of new stars.
items.sourceMeaning:
The loosely spread gas is heated in the crossing too. It spreads into a broad bridge, too diffuse and hot to collapse promptly into stars. Different parts of this great volume will meet other clouds along the way.

*A broad bridge of hot gas*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Gas drawn out of the outer spiral
items.subject: The outer cloud's three lobes drawn into an uneven long hooked ribbon.
items.distinction: Retain its curved shoulder; avoid shredding into solid rocks or a comet nucleus.
items.sourceMeaning:
This outer cloud misses the main gas collision. The unequal pull of the approaching galaxy stretches its surroundings and draws gas outward with the stars.

Matter can leave a spiral arm without first being burned or broken.

*Gas drawn out of the outer spiral*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Outskirts of the other galaxy
items.subject: Open arcs of sparse stellar stipple extending beyond the target's edges; far-separated points.
items.distinction: No central star cluster, flame, shock front or future remnant.

fixedAssets.variantPolicy: Reuse registered source only where camera and creation state match.

items.sourceMeaning: Stars fill this immense region sparsely. The approaching galaxy can bend their journeys without bringing their surfaces together. Its pull also differs across an extended cloud, stretching the cloud and drawing material beyond the old spiral.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Stars around an old orange star
items.subject: One orange stellar point among five smaller pale points in a gently bent loose strand; ample black gaps.
items.distinction: The orange light is a star, not a burning planet; the five neighbors are a recognition shorthand, not an exact census.
items.sourceMeaning: The orange star has already shone for billions of years. Its neighbours share this part of the spiral, with immense spaces between them.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dense gas in the dark lane
items.subject: An opaque branching dark ribbon with a large fork and three broad knots, faint dusty edge against a brighter sparse stellar field.
items.distinction: Extinction means material blocks background light; do not make the dark lane an empty crack in space.
items.sourceMeaning: An extended cloud of gas, threaded with inherited dust. Its darkest parts contain dense knots; much of its material is more loosely spread.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Gas crossing the dark lane
items.subject: A broad oblique pale gas ribbon with a scalloped leading edge, approaching the dark ribbon's orientation.
items.distinction: A second extended gas reservoir, not another dark-lane clone or a solid projectile.
items.sourceMeaning: Gas from the other spiral moves into the lane. Unlike the stars, these extended clouds occupy much of the space through which they pass.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Thin gas beside the dark lane
items.subject: Widely spread wisps with large open gaps and no compact central knot.
items.distinction: Thin gas must differ in filling and texture from dense cloud, beyond a color change.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A cloud beyond the gas crossing
items.subject: An off-centre three-lobed cloud with a narrow curved shoulder, outside the crowded lane.
items.distinction: Keep its shoulder into the stretched tail family; it misses the main collision.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Young stars from the dark lane
items.subject: An asymmetrical fan of separated blue-white and warm pale stellar points, three modest long-lived anchor lights among brighter early members and residual dark dust at one edge.
items.distinction: Do not reuse tail-cluster triangle; population, not one star with sparkles.
items.sourceMeaning: The cold ribbon feeds many contracting centres, where falling matter releases light. As they gather more gas, their cores become hot enough for sustained hydrogen fusion to support the new stars. Dust still hides much of their light. The most massive will shine brilliantly and die early; smaller members can endure for billions of years.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

proposedPresentationVariants.subject: The same surviving open stellar fan with three modest long-lived anchor lights, redistributed and less dominated by bright blue stars; early massive members are absent.
proposedPresentationVariants.distinction: Ageing changes membership before the final crossing. This is the actual earlier population, not fresh star formation.
proposedPresentationVariants.status: proposed artwork metadata, not present in canonical manuscript
proposedPresentationVariants.scope: from chapter is a global current-presentation change, including earlier panels; review scrollback accordingly

items.name: Young star with a dusty disk
items.subject: One cream-white young star shining through contraction inside a broad dusty elliptical disk, a dark near-side notch and asymmetric hooked outer rim.
items.distinction: Keep the host recognizable through its own disk appearances; sustained fusion begins later, so no visual ignition threshold or completed planets, rings or mature moon yet. The host is never absorbed into the later world-and-moon icons.

fixedAssets.variantPolicy: Reuse registered source only where camera and creation state match.

items.sourceMeaning: The smaller turning knot contracts into a shining young star. Some incoming gas keeps circling, carrying inherited dust into its disk. The star will later settle into sustained hydrogen fusion; its planet-forming surroundings already exist. Here, matter from the dark lane continues circling outside the new light.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Cold gas entering the large gathering
items.subject: A narrow cool dark filament entering a broad gathering, with two dense knots separated by opaque gas.
items.distinction: Large-gathering gas; no newborn stars in the supply.
items.sourceMeaning: A long ribbon of cold gas enters a broad part of the crowded lane. Within that region, many centres are beginning to gather material.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dusty gas entering the small turning knot
items.subject: A narrower dusty curling filament with grain-bearing opaque streaks, directed around a small empty centre.
items.distinction: Distinct from large cold ribbon by tight curl and scale context; no complete disk or star yet.
items.sourceMeaning: Gas and inherited solid grains flow toward the smaller knot. The dust was already mixed through the cloud before the galaxies met.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A thin cloud fringe
items.subject: A diffuse curved fringe with an irregular inner edge and sparse transparent wisps.
items.distinction: The same fringe can glow from radiation or a jet; do not prepaint either result.
items.sourceMeaning: Separate portions fringe the nursery and cross the smaller star's outgoing jet. Light can reach this gas; fast material can strike it too.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Gas glowing around the new stars
items.subject: A broad irregular translucent glow along the old fringe's inner edge, dark dust surviving behind it.
items.distinction: Photoionized gas differs geometrically from the compact jet bow; no new stellar population.
items.sourceMeaning:
Radiation from the hottest young stars reaches the thin cloud fringe. Hydrogen loses electrons and shines as electrons are captured again. The stars have made part of their old surroundings luminous.

*Gas glowing around the new stars*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Glowing gas where the jet strikes
items.subject: A bent bright bow where the narrow stream meets a cloud, with broken glowing gas behind the curved front.
items.distinction: Shock-lit gas remains extended; avoid star-shaped points standing for new stars.
items.sourceMeaning:
Gas in the narrow stream crashes into the cloud in its path. The shock heats the struck gas, making it glow where the stream meets it. These lights come from hot gas rather than another group of stars.

*Glowing gas where the jet strikes*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Gas flowing out of the nursery
items.subject: A wide asymmetric fan of gas with streaked inner filaments expanding into diffuse outskirts.
items.distinction: Broader than narrow jet; outward arrangement must not imply a new star or consumed entire nursery.
items.sourceMeaning:
The young stars heat the loose cloud, and their outflows drive into it. The gas expands and is swept away from the nursery; much of it will never become a star here. Beyond the new lights, this continuing flow meets the galaxy's wider gas.

*Gas flowing out of the nursery*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dense cloud pillars
items.subject: Three unequal dark pillars rooted in a ragged cloud bank, bright eroding edges and dense sheltered interiors.
items.distinction: No stone columns or vegetation; not every bit of the original cloud remains.
items.sourceMeaning:
The dense cloud's exposed surface erodes, but its thick interior shields material behind it. Dark pillars of gas remain where the surroundings have been cleared more quickly. Their exposed edges continue to wear away.

*Dense cloud pillars*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Gas falling toward the growing stars
items.subject: Several smooth gas filaments converging from above, no solid grain specks or destination body.
items.distinction: A gas reservoir, not the process of falling or a gravity arrow.
items.sourceMeaning: A continuing supply, divided among the established growing bodies. Some joins stars; some is redirected into outflows.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dusty gas falling into the smaller system
items.subject: Similar converging gas with embedded clotted dark dust ribbons, narrowed toward the same disk plane.
items.distinction: Texture and geometry distinguish dusty supply; do not show survivable solid grains inside hot jet launch.
items.sourceMeaning: Dusty gas continues falling toward the smaller star and disk. Some feeds their growth; some gas is redirected into their jet. The grains need not survive the hot launching region.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A narrow stream of gas from the young star
items.subject: A narrow material column with a bright inner knot and two weak shock knots, leaving the young disk's axis.
items.distinction: A protostellar outflow, no rocket, laser, floating force or black-hole shadow.
items.sourceMeaning:
While gas continues to fall toward the young star, part is launched outward in a narrow jet. Magnetic fields near the star and disk help guide that outflow. The growing system sends some of its incoming matter back into the cloud.

*A narrow stream of gas from the young star*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A loose cloud beside the stars
items.subject: Loose rounded wisps with thin edges and large gaps beside a common illumination direction.
items.distinction: Do not equate pale tint with a particular temperature; thin structure is the useful cue.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A dense cloud beside the stars
items.subject: A solid-looking three-pronged dark gas mass with thick opaque roots and a scalloped exposed edge.
items.distinction: Material is gas and dust, not rock; this supplies the recognizable pillar roots.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Gas in the long tail
items.subject: The hooked outer ribbon now with a thicker three-lobed gas gathering along its base.
items.distinction: Retain a-outer-cloud shoulder; distinguish from the unrelated nursery outflow.
items.sourceMeaning:
The stretched outer cloud gathers with cold gas moving along the tail. The encounter has carried this material beyond the former bright extent of the spiral. Near the tail's base it meets gas driven out of the nursery, arriving by a different route.

*Gas in the long tail*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A dense knot at the tail's base
items.subject: A compact irregular knot enclosing the three recognizable dense lobes in newly gathered gas.
items.distinction: Still gaseous, not a complete star cluster.
items.sourceMeaning:
Cold gas gathers around the clumps carried from the old pillars. Material that resisted the first clearing becomes part of a new gathering outside the old nursery.

*A dense knot at the tail's base*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Mixed gas dispersed into the outer galaxy
items.subject: An extremely diffuse uneven haze with dispersed threads and almost no closed boundary.
items.distinction: Distinguish from a compact cold cloud by lack of knots; do not imply matter vanished.
items.sourceMeaning:
Material from the outward stream, including gas it can strip from the tail, meets the thin outer gas and spreads. The clear outline of a cloud disappears. Its ingredients remain distributed through the galaxy's surroundings, where different portions can have later encounters.

*Mixed gas dispersed into the outer galaxy*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: The galaxy's thin, hot outer gas
items.subject: Open broad contour fragments around a very sparse field, with thin gas hatching between stars.
items.distinction: No solid boundary, sphere wall, cloud-sized finite halo or cold central knot.

items.sourceMeaning: A broad region beyond the bright disk. It contains gas, though far less densely than the dark clouds in the spiral.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Cold gas flowing along the tail
items.subject: A long narrow cool filament parallel to the tail curve, with uneven dense beads of gas.
items.distinction: Beads remain diffuse clumps, not stars; material already occupies the tail.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Nursery gas mixed into the outer stream
items.subject: A wide streaming fan with one smooth bridge-like band crossing its finer nursery filaments.
items.distinction: Mixed origins need not produce magic two-color stripes; name supplies provenance.
items.sourceMeaning:
Material driven out by young stars meets a portion of the hot bridge made in the first galactic crossing. Their collision and mixing bring those two histories together.

A familiar-looking cloud need not have a single origin.

*Nursery gas mixed into the outer stream*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Gas stripped from the tail cloud's edge
items.subject: A ragged detached plume with two dense wisps drawn from the tail's curved shoulder.
items.distinction: A selected edge portion, not a second whole tail or a solid torn strip.
items.sourceMeaning:
Where the outward stream meets the tail cloud, exposed material is torn away and mixed into the flow. Most of the cloud continues along the tail, while its stripped edge travels with the outgoing gas.

*Gas stripped from the tail cloud's edge*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dense clumps carried out of the nursery
items.subject: Three unequal dark clumps corresponding to the old pillar heads, with eroded trailing veils.
items.distinction: Retain relative large-medium-small shape hierarchy without preserving impossible whole pillars.
items.sourceMeaning:
The outward flow erodes the old pillars and carries surviving clumps into the nearby tail-base region. They retain dense interiors for this part of their journey.

*Dense clumps carried out of the nursery*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Young stars at the tail's base
items.subject: A compact triangular group of separated points with a smaller warm cluster offset at its base and residual gas.
items.distinction: The grouping distinguishes it from the lane's open fan; exact membership is schematic.

fixedAssets.variantPolicy: Reuse registered source only where camera and creation state match.
Reuse registered source only where camera and creation state match.

items.sourceMeaning:
The knot containing the old pillars' surviving clumps gathers with its neighbouring cold cloud. Over millions of years, part of this material contracts and begins sustained fusion, while surrounding gas remains outside the new stars. Clumps that endured the nursery's clearing have helped make new lights beyond its edge.

*Young stars at the tail's base*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dust warmed by the dark-lane stars
items.subject: The curved dusty veil now subtly warm within its surviving grain-rich patches, no point stars in the cloud.
items.distinction: Infrared warmth is a declared illustrative color convention, not naked-eye red-hot dust.
items.sourceMeaning:
Near the original nursery, a portion of the dusty gas absorbs light from the stars born in the dark lane. Its grains warm and radiate much of that energy at infrared wavelengths.

Gas can glow because its atoms are excited; solid grains can shine by radiating absorbed heat. Neither light requires another star to have formed in the cloud.

*Dust warmed by the dark-lane stars*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Outward gas with much of its dust destroyed
items.subject: A diffuse fan retaining the outflow curve but with greatly reduced dense grain patches.
items.distinction: Do not show zero matter or an absolutely dust-free cloud; extent of depletion is textual.
items.sourceMeaning:
Dust carried outward enters the hot outer surroundings. Collisions with fast particles gradually erode many grains, returning their material to the gas. Prior warming by starlight does not protect a grain from this later erosion.

Of the inherited solids, some remain in the young star's disk, some are warmed near the nursery, and some cease to be solid grains.

*Outward gas with much of its dust destroyed*
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A cold cloud beside the tail knot
items.subject: A dense kidney-shaped dark cloud with a short pale rim beside the tail knot.
items.distinction: Distinct supply, not the tail knot reproduced.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dusty gas near the nursery's outskirts
items.subject: A curved dusty veil containing irregular dark grain-rich patches and a broad translucent fringe.
items.distinction: Inherited dust mixed through gas; no new star or stone gravel pile.
items.sourceMeaning: Different portions of this broad dusty region lie near the stars and in the path of their outflow. The grains are inherited material, not newly manufactured dust.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dust carried with the outward gas
items.subject: A streaming gas fan containing dark clotted grains, with sheltered dense knots inside the flow.
items.distinction: Dust is carried material; it is not flame sparks or all destroyed already.
items.sourceMeaning: Outgoing gas overtakes the dusty material and carries grains with it. Some grains remain sheltered inside denser clumps for part of this journey; others become exposed as the flow erodes those clumps. Dust that was warmed by starlight can join the same outward journey.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Rocky pebbles
items.subject: Three compact irregular rounded pebbles with closed, solid surfaces.
items.distinction: Denser than porous clumps; not full spherical worlds.
items.sourceMeaning: Repeated gentle encounters build these dry grains into compact pebbles. They are still small bodies, held together where their grains touch; further sticking alone cannot carry them all the way to planets.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Grains from shattered clumps
items.subject: Dispersed angular fragments with remnants of the former lacy aggregate at one side.
items.distinction: Destructive fragmentation, not evaporation, smoke or returned identical intact clump.
items.sourceMeaning: The fast grains strike the fragile gatherings. Much of their apparent growth comes apart: the same solid material is again divided among smaller pieces.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Clumps rebuilt from fragments
items.subject: New lacy aggregates containing angular chips and finer adherent dust, an arrangement unlike the original clumps.
items.distinction: Same material lineage, not resurrection of the original unique shape.
items.sourceMeaning: Broken grains meet fresh dust gently enough to stick again. The fragments gather into new loose clumps, returning some of the shattered material to larger forms.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Warm inner disk
items.subject: Two open elliptical arcs showing the inner band of the established young disk and its starward edge.
items.distinction: No glowing sun duplicate or freestanding heat icon; no preformed pebbles.

fixedAssets.variantPolicy: Reuse registered source only where camera and creation state match.

items.sourceMeaning: The smaller star's warm inner disk. Rock grains can remain here where their ice coatings cannot.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dust falling into the disk
items.subject: A sparse descending fan of tiny angular grains within faint gas, aligned toward the young disk plane.
items.distinction: Representative enlarged grains, not a shower of planet-sized boulders.
items.sourceMeaning: These inherited grains arrived with the gas that formed the smaller star. A little of that continuing inflow is still falling toward its disk.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Slowly meeting grains
items.subject: Separated small angular dry grains with gently converging spacing and several near contacts.
items.distinction: Slow relative motion cannot be proven by a still image; distinguish spatial pattern and preserve name.
items.sourceMeaning: A neighboring supply of grains moving gently relative to one another. Several portions can take part in local encounters.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Fast crossing grains
items.subject: A narrow oblique train of the same small angular grains crossing empty space.
items.distinction: No flame or velocity token; motion direction is contextual and must survive without invented arrows.
items.sourceMeaning: A narrow stream crossing the slower material. Its speed relative to the loose clumps makes their collisions destructive.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Ice-coated grains moving inward
items.subject: Irregular rock grains with visibly pale rounded frost mantles, a few in an inward-curving chain.
items.distinction: Ice is a coating on grains, not blue gemstones or droplets.
items.sourceMeaning: These grains began farther out in this same disk. Gas drag is carrying them toward its warmer region.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Dust settled into the disk
items.subject: A thin broad horizontal band of fine grains with a denser central plane and diffuse grains above it.
items.distinction: A settled reservoir, not a single clump or a completed rocky body.
items.sourceMeaning: The falling grains join the existing disk. Drag against its gas changes their motion, and much of this material settles toward the disk's crowded middle plane. Here, fresh grains mingle with fragments from earlier collisions.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Fluffy grain clumps
items.subject: Two or three open lacy aggregates of angular grains with large internal voids.
items.distinction: Keep visible porosity; not compact stone pebbles.
items.sourceMeaning: Gentle encounters let small grains stick in open, fragile gatherings. They are not yet stones, and a harder encounter can undo them.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Grains stripped of their ice
items.subject: The dark irregular grain cores from b-icy-grains without thick pale mantles.
items.distinction: Names may be needed versus generic dry dust; no liquid puddle or disappearing rocky cores.
items.sourceMeaning: As the inward-moving grains enter the warm disk, their ice evaporates into the surrounding gas. The rocky grains remain. The lost ice has changed phase, not vanished.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Shattered ice-coated grains
items.subject: Smaller broken angular grain cores with patchy retained pale frost around their edges.
items.distinction: Retain visible ice unlike b-dry-grains; fragmentation has not sublimated the coatings.
items.sourceMeaning: A fast encounter breaks the incoming icy grains before they reach the warm region. Smaller fragments still carry ice; fragmentation and evaporation are different ways to change the same material.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: The rocky world with a small moon
items.subject: The same muted rocky sphere with one small distinct grey moon separated by a readable gap; a broad inherited impact basin.
items.distinction: Moon remains much smaller; not Earth, ocean or Saturn-like rings.
items.sourceMeaning: Orbiting rubble meets the impact debris. Far enough from the world for loose clumps to hold together, repeated collisions and gravitational gathering build a small moon. Other fragments fall back or escape.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A small world held together as rubble
items.subject: A squat asymmetric bean-shaped aggregate, one deep notch and three large visible constituent boulders including a pale wedge.
items.distinction: This unique aggregate persists intact even after it loses its sun; no conventional smooth asteroid substitution.
items.sourceMeaning: Some of the shattered body's fragments meet a slowly approaching rocky body. Repeated low-speed collisions and gravity gather them into a loose, bound world. Other fragments remain scattered between the planets.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Small bodies approaching slowly
items.subject: Three small lumpy solid bodies at modest separation on converging oblique alignments.
items.distinction: A supply of bodies; still image does not establish speed without name and context.
items.sourceMeaning: Rocky bodies travel on gently converging paths. Some approach the growing world; others cross clouds of fragments. Their low relative speeds favour encounters that retain much of the arriving mass.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Large worlds approaching at different angles
items.subject: Two distinct larger rocky globes approaching at visibly different angles, one more direct and one grazing the common contextual orientation.
items.distinction: Different population members and approach angles; neither is the followed unique world, and the same impactor is not reused.
items.sourceMeaning: Large rocky bodies cross the inner disk on different paths. Some approach the growing world more directly; others graze its edge.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Metal-rich rocky fragments
items.subject: Angular dark metallic grains among rocky chips, broad specular facets but no polished manufactured metal.
items.distinction: Inherited metal-bearing material, not fresh stellar product or iron ingots.
items.sourceMeaning: Fragments rich in metal, inherited with the disk's other solids. They carry material made before this young star was born.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Fast rocky projectiles
items.subject: A sparse narrow train of compact jagged stones with sharply separated silhouettes.
items.distinction: Fast relative speed is context; do not use fire trails or make them identical to slow supplies by tint alone.
items.sourceMeaning: A population of fast stones and smaller rocky bodies crossing the inner worlds and debris. Individual portions strike different targets; survivors remain among the planets for later encounters.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: Rubble already orbiting the struck world
items.subject: An open curved segment of separated rocky pieces at similar spacing, suggesting the tracked world's orbital plane.
items.distinction: Only the supplied rubble; no second copy of the whole world or already gathered moon.
items.sourceMeaning: A small supply of rubble already circles the rocky world. It moves in the same direction as the impact debris, with relative speeds low enough for repeated collisions to gather material.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A population of rocky bodies
items.subject: Several closed rocky bodies of unequal sizes, rounded larger members and irregular smaller members.
items.distinction: Unlike loose grain clumps; no single hero world yet.
items.sourceMeaning: Rocky pebbles mingle with fragments or rebuilt clumps in a crowded, gas-rich band. Drag between gas and solids concentrates them until dense patches collapse under their own gravity. Many rocky bodies emerge, large enough to hold other matter nearby.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: A young rocky world
items.subject: One muted plum-grey rocky sphere with a broad dark crescent, uneven youthful surface and a chipped-looking light rim.
items.distinction: Carry palette, illumination and hemisphere orientation through the sequence; mutable geology is not a permanent logo.
items.sourceMeaning: One of the newly formed rocky bodies meets a slower incoming body and keeps much of its material. Through this and further encounters, it grows into a rocky world.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: The rocky world with a molten interior
items.subject: The same larger world with a small consistent diagrammatic interior wedge revealing irregular molten layers.
items.distinction: Cutaway is an explanatory convention, not a literal missing slice; do not make surface glow prove whole-world melting.
items.sourceMeaning: A large rocky body strikes the growing world, leaving much of its material behind. The impact releases enough energy to melt a substantial part of the enlarged world's interior.
items.reviewStatus: planned; no artwork generated or reviewed

items.name: The rocky world with a dense core
items.subject: The same world and cutaway orientation, now showing one dense inner core beneath lighter rocky layers.
items.distinction: Differentiate from surface metal rubble; core state cannot be inferred from a normal exterior view.
items.sourceMeaning: Metal-rich fragments join the hot world. Within its molten regions, dense metal sinks while lighter rock remains above. As the material settles and the world loses heat, a dense core takes shape.

chapters.intro:
The winding arms are gone. So is the dark lane by which the cloud could once be followed.

The old orange star remains. So do stars made from that cloud and the cluster born beyond the spiral. The younger sun still carries its moon-bearing rocky world and ringed giant; the small rubble world travels without that sun. Between them lies material that has been heated, scattered, gathered and given light more than once.

Their shared galaxy did not exist when any of those journeys began. It contains what survived the encounter, and what the encounter made possible.
